stories.headline: Free weekly running sessions offered at Wisbech Park
stories.brief:
Residents across the Fens are being invited to join a free, weekly running programme at Wisbech Park. Organised by Active Fenland, the Couch to 5k sessions take place every Tuesday morning between 9:30am and 10:30am. 

The group is led by England Athletics-qualified coach Gary Bligh and is open to all abilities, regardless of previous running experience. Organisers say the sessions focus on building confidence and stamina in a supportive environment, with no pressure to meet specific pace targets. Beyond the physical exercise, the group offers a social opportunity for participants to meet new people. Those interested in taking part can simply turn up to the park to get involved.

stories.headline: Battle of Britain commemoration service in King’s Lynn
stories.brief:
A wreath-laying ceremony will be held in King’s Lynn’s Tower Gardens this Monday to mark the 86th anniversary of the Battle of Britain. The service begins at 10:45am and will be led by the Reverend Canon Mark Dimond. West Norfolk Mayor, Councillor Steve Bearshaw, is expected to attend alongside representatives from the Armed Forces, local schools, and cadet groups.

The event also signals the launch of the Royal Air Forces Association’s annual Wings Appeal. Organisers are encouraging veterans and members of the public to attend the commemoration. Following the service, guests are invited to Marriotts Warehouse for refreshments.

stories.headline: Major rail disruption in Ely following person hit by train
stories.brief: Rail services across Cambridgeshire are facing significant disruption today following reports that a person has been struck by a train in Ely. Passengers are being advised to expect major delays and potential cancellations while emergency services respond to the incident. Those planning to travel through the area should check the latest service updates before heading to the station, as the situation is currently impacting the wider rail network. Further information regarding the resumption of normal services will be provided as it becomes available.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire man shares 9/11 experience in Newfoundland
stories.brief: A Cambridgeshire resident has spoken about his experience during the September 11 attacks. Gary Christy, who was a passenger at the time, has shared his story of receiving kindness while stranded in Newfoundland. The account highlights the support he encountered in the region following the events of that day.

stories.headline: Metrion Biosciences staff cycle 112 miles for youth charity
stories.brief: Staff from the Cambridgeshire-based firm Metrion Biosciences are undertaking a 112-mile cycling challenge today to raise funds for the charity Centre 33. The team is visiting all five of the charity’s hubs, including the site in Wisbech, as well as locations in Peterborough, Huntingdon, and Ely. The ride aims to support the organisation’s work providing mental health and practical assistance to young people aged 13 to 25. Colleagues are also contributing to the fundraising effort by using static bikes at the company's offices. Last year, Centre 33 provided support to nearly 4,000 young people across the region.

stories.headline: Repairs underway following burst water main in King’s Lynn
stories.brief:
A burst water main continues to cause flooding at the Tuesday Market Place in King’s Lynn today. The leak, which was first reported yesterday morning, has resulted in standing water across the town centre, with motorists seen driving through the affected area. 

Anglian Water crews are currently on site working to resolve the issue. The utility company expects the repairs to be completed by 1pm today. Local councillor Rob Colwell has described the incident as frustrating for residents who are being asked to conserve water during the current drought. While West Norfolk Council has confirmed that local facilities remain open, commuters are advised to take care when travelling through the town centre.

stories.headline: Prison inmate sentenced for organising Lincolnshire burglary
stories.brief: A man has been sentenced for coordinating a burglary at a storage site in Lincolnshire while serving time in prison. The individual used his cell to organise the criminal activity. No further details regarding the location of the storage site or the length of the sentence have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire County Council cuts funding for handyperson service
stories.brief:
Cambridgeshire County Council has confirmed it is withdrawing funding for the local handyperson service. The decision, which has been highlighted by Age UK, will impact the availability of support for residents who rely on the scheme for home maintenance tasks. 

The service has historically provided assistance to older people across the region. Residents are advised that this change in council policy will affect the future delivery of these provisions. Further details regarding the timeline for the withdrawal of the service have not been provided at this stage.

stories.headline: Petition launched to protect services at King’s Lynn hospital
stories.brief:
A petition to save key departments at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn has reached 7,000 signatures. Residents are concerned about reports that the hospital’s Accident and Emergency, intensive care, and maternity units could face a downgrade. 

Local politicians are seeking urgent meetings with the Norfolk and Waveney University Hospitals Group to demand clarity. While the hospital group insists that no decisions have been made regarding future service configurations, they are currently developing a long-term clinical strategy for the region. A spokesperson confirmed that any potential changes would require public consultation. The hospital is set to discuss its future at an annual members’ meeting this Thursday, which is open to the public.

stories.headline: Details sought on Peterborough's £40m Pride in Place scheme
stories.brief: Residents are looking for more information regarding the forty-million-pound Pride in Place project in Peterborough. The initiative, which has been highlighted by the BBC, aims to invest significant funding into the local area. At this stage, specific details on how the money will be allocated or the timeline for the work remain limited. We will continue to monitor for further updates on how this investment might impact the wider Fenland region as more information becomes available.

stories.headline: New bereavement centre opens in East Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: A new facility for those experiencing bereavement has opened in East Cambridgeshire. The centre is situated by a lakeside, providing a dedicated space for support within the local community. Further details regarding the services available at the site have not been released.

stories.headline: Spalding fire station targeted by thieves
stories.brief: Police are investigating after Spalding fire station was targeted by thieves. The incident at the town’s station has been reported by the Spalding South Holland News. No further details regarding the items taken or the timing of the theft have been released at this stage.

stories.headline: Neale-Wade Academy trust issued formal warning
stories.brief: The trust responsible for the Neale-Wade Academy has been issued a formal warning regarding its performance. Officials have stated that the organisation must show significant improvement or face the possibility of being removed from its position overseeing the school. No further details regarding the specific nature of the concerns or the timeline for these improvements have been released at this stage.

stories.headline: College of West Anglia hosts annual Freshers’ Fair
stories.brief:
Hundreds of new students have marked the start of the academic year at the College of West Anglia in King’s Lynn. The two-day Freshers’ Fair introduced learners to a variety of local charities, businesses, and support services. 

Representatives from organisations including the Samaritans, the Benjamin Foundation, and West Norfolk Council attended the event to engage with the student body. The fair is a key part of the college’s induction programme, designed to help new arrivals settle into college life, connect with the local community, and discover opportunities beyond their studies.

stories.headline: Preparations underway for 2025 Pilgrim Hospital Christmas Convoy
stories.brief: Organisers have officially started the countdown for the 2025 Christmas Convoy heading to Pilgrim Hospital in Boston. Planning is now underway for the annual event, which sees a procession of vehicles travel to the site during the festive season. Further details regarding the schedule and how the public can get involved are expected to be released as the date approaches.

stories.headline: Fenland District Council to sell former Barclays bank site in March
stories.brief: Fenland District Council has reached an agreement to sell the former Barclays bank building located in March. The decision follows reports from the BBC regarding the future of the site. No further details regarding the sale price or the identity of the buyer have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Water leak causes disruption in King’s Lynn town centre
stories.brief:
Drivers in King’s Lynn are facing travel disruption this morning following a water leak at the Tuesday Market Place. The leak has resulted in a large pool of water forming on the road directly outside the Alive Corn Exchange. 

Engineers from Anglian Water are currently on-site carrying out repairs to address low-pressure issues in the area. West Norfolk Council has confirmed that the nearby public toilets on Ferry Street are closed while the work is underway. Motorists are advised to take care when navigating the area.

stories.headline: Peterborough Museum prehistoric collection receives new status
stories.brief: The prehistoric collection at Peterborough Museum has been granted a new official status. The announcement follows reports from the Peterborough Fenland Edge News regarding the museum's historical exhibits. No further details have been provided at this time regarding the specific nature of the classification.

stories.headline: Weekend activities listed for Cambridge area
stories.brief: Residents looking for plans this weekend can choose from a selection of eight activities in and around Cambridge. The list, published by the Cambridge Independent, highlights various local options for those in the region. Anyone interested in finding out more about what is happening nearby can view the full details on the Cambridge Independent website.

stories.headline: Nazi symbol scratched onto RAF sign
stories.brief: Police are investigating after a Nazi symbol was found scratched onto an RAF sign. The incident has been described as deplorable by those reporting on the vandalism. No further details regarding the location of the sign or the timing of the damage have been released at this stage. Authorities are appealing for anyone with information regarding the incident to come forward.

stories.headline: Wimblington golf centre issues statement following death of seven-year-old boy
stories.brief: A golf centre in Wimblington has described the death of a seven-year-old boy as heartbreaking. The venue released a statement following the incident, though no further details regarding the circumstances have been provided at this time.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn adult entertainment club seeks move to larger premises
stories.brief:
The owner of the King’s Lynn gentleman’s club, 7th Heaven, has applied for a new sexual entertainment licence to relocate to larger premises. Ian Cunliffe is seeking permission to move the business from its current Norfolk Street location to the second floor of the nearby Rewind nightclub. 

If the application is approved, the owner intends to provide more dance space and an improved bar area. The club currently operates from Thursday to Saturday, between 9pm and 4am. The proposal is open for public consultation until September 25. Residents wishing to comment on the application should write to the Licensing department at the Borough Council of King’s Lynn and West Norfolk.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire police conduct county lines crackdown
stories.brief: Cambridgeshire Constabulary has carried out a series of arrests as part of a targeted operation against county lines drug activity. The police force confirmed that action was taken to disrupt the illegal supply networks operating across the region. No further details regarding the specific locations of the arrests or the number of individuals detained have been released at this time. Residents are encouraged to report any suspicious activity to the police as efforts to tackle these criminal operations continue.

stories.headline: Support project for Armed Forces community launched in King’s Lynn
stories.brief:
A new initiative called Project Nourish and Connect is offering support to the Armed Forces community in King’s Lynn. Run by The Bridge for Heroes, the scheme aims to combat loneliness by providing home-cooked meals and a space for social interaction six days a week.

The drop-in centre, located on South Clough Lane, is open Monday to Friday from 10am until 3pm, and on Saturdays between 10am and 2pm. The project is funded by the Norfolk Community Foundation. Members of the Armed Forces community interested in the service can visit the centre in person or call 01553 760230 for further information.

stories.headline: Peterborough Museum prehistoric collection receives new status
stories.brief: The prehistoric collection held at Peterborough Museum has been granted a new official status. The announcement follows reports from the Peterborough Fenland Edge News regarding the site's historical exhibits. No further details have been provided at this time regarding the nature of the designation or how it will affect future displays.

stories.headline: Lincolnshire regeneration plan approved
stories.brief: A major regeneration project aimed at improving towns across Lincolnshire has been granted official approval. The ambitious vision, which focuses on development and enhancement within the county, has now been given the green light. Further details regarding the specific impact on local areas are expected to follow as the plans progress.

stories.headline: Two men convicted of hare coursing offences
stories.brief: Two men have been found guilty of attending a hare coursing event. The conviction follows an investigation by Cambridgeshire Constabulary. No further details regarding the individuals or the location of the incident have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Police investigate dog attack in Wisbech Park
stories.brief:
Police are appealing for information following a dog attack in Wisbech Park yesterday evening. Officers were called to the scene at approximately 6pm after a 12-year-old boy sustained minor injuries. The child was taken to hospital for treatment. 

Authorities have launched an investigation into the incident, which is being treated as a case of allowing a dog to be dangerously out of control. No arrests have been made at this stage. Anyone who may have witnessed the event or possesses relevant CCTV footage is asked to contact Cambridgeshire Police via their website, quoting reference 35/69822/26.

stories.headline: Man hospitalised after incident on London Road in King’s Lynn
stories.brief: A man has been taken to the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn following an incident on London Road yesterday evening. Police were called to the scene at 7:58pm after reports of a man lying in the road. Officers attended the location and spoke with the individual before he was transported to the hospital by ambulance. Authorities have confirmed that the man sustained minor injuries. Police enquiries are currently ongoing to determine the circumstances surrounding the event.

stories.headline: Historic Fenland venues open doors for Heritage Open Days
stories.brief:
Residents across the Fens are invited to explore local history as part of the annual National Heritage Open Days. Over the next two weekends, various sites in Wisbech and March will offer free public access and guided tours.

In March, visitors can view the railway station heritage room or the Masonic Centre. Wisbech venues participating include Peckover House, the Town Hall, and the Fenland Museum. Other highlights include tours of the Tydd Pumping Station, the General Cemetery, and the St Peter and St Paul Church. Opening times and dates vary by location, with events running across September 12, 13, 19, and 20. Full details on specific opening hours for each venue are available through local listings.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn parkrun celebrates 15th anniversary
stories.brief:
Hundreds of people gathered at The Walks in King’s Lynn this weekend to mark the 15th anniversary of the local parkrun. A total of 430 participants took part in the weekly 5k event, which first launched in September 2011 with just 61 runners.

Following the anniversary run, 150 participants took on a 24-hour endurance challenge, completing a combined total of 1,050 miles. Event director Gary Walker thanked the Terrington St Clement Running Club for their volunteer support throughout the weekend. The parkrun remains a free, volunteer-led event open to people of all ages and abilities.

stories.headline: Students highlight local benefits of ARU Peterborough
stories.brief: Students at ARU Peterborough have reported that the university is providing new opportunities closer to their homes. According to reports, those attending the institution feel that having the facility in the city has made higher education more accessible. The feedback suggests that the presence of the university is helping local learners pursue their academic goals without the need to travel further afield.

stories.headline: Changes announced for number 31 bus services
stories.brief: Passengers using the number 31 bus service are being warned of upcoming changes to their journeys. According to reports from the Ely East Cambridgeshire News, the service is facing a shake-up that will include alterations to existing timetables. In addition to these scheduling adjustments, some bus stops are set to be dropped from the route. Commuters are advised to check for updated information regarding their specific stops and travel times before planning their journeys.

stories.headline: Lincolnshire family shares diagnosis story
stories.brief: A family in Lincolnshire has spoken out after a relative received a serious medical diagnosis. Relatives initially believed the man was suffering from seasonal blues before his condition was identified. The story, reported by Lincolnshire Live, highlights the family's experience following the unexpected health news.

stories.headline: Concerns raised over proposed energy plant in Chatteris
stories.brief: Residents in Chatteris have expressed concerns regarding a proposed energy plant for the town. Local reports indicate that fears have been raised about the potential for unpleasant odours resulting from the development. No further details regarding the planning application or the nature of the facility have been confirmed at this stage.

stories.headline: Changes proposed for Fenland bus services
stories.brief:
Plans to alter 31 bus routes across Cambridgeshire have been presented to the Combined Authority’s transport committee. The report, titled “Bus Services Reimagined,” includes proposals to redesign services 56 and T7 in Fenland. Officials state these changes would improve connections between March and Wisbech by offering earlier and later journeys, alongside increased weekend availability. Additionally, timetables for services 46 and 50 may be adjusted, affecting routes through Chatteris and villages near Wisbech.

The committee met on Wednesday to discuss the recommendations, which include various timetable changes and stop removals. If the Combined Authority’s board approves the proposals, the first stage of the new bus network is scheduled to begin in February 2027.

stories.headline: Debate continues over Norfolk County Council ward funding cuts
stories.brief:
Norfolk County Council’s Reform leadership is facing criticism following the decision to scrap the local members’ fund in June. The £924,000 pot previously allowed councillors to spend £11,000 each on local highways improvements. Liberal Democrat councillor Rob Colwell, who represents Gaywood North, highlighted the impact of the cuts by showcasing a recently completed £3,000 project to install safety bollards outside Churchill Park Academy.

However, cabinet member for highways and transport, Tom Dickerson, has defended the move. He stated that centralising the budget allows the council to prioritise essential road maintenance, such as fixing potholes. He added that other funding remains available for smaller local schemes, and the change is intended to provide better value for money across the county.

stories.headline: Norfolk council reorganisation plans paused by Government
stories.brief:
Plans to reorganise local government in Norfolk have been put on hold by the Government. The review, which aimed to split the county into three councils, has been paused by Housing Secretary Angela Rayner to ensure the correct process is followed.

Local representatives have expressed frustration over the move, citing the loss of time and money already invested in the project. Norfolk County Council’s deputy leader, Councillor Robin Hunter-Clarke, says the authority has spent £1.2 million on the process and is calling for the Government to reimburse these costs. While the Government remains committed to the reorganisation, officials expect to provide a further update on the project’s future in the coming months.

stories.headline: Looking back at West Norfolk headlines from 1986
stories.brief:
This week we look back at the news from September 1986. Campaigners in Boughton held a silent protest to save their village school during the Best Kept Village Award presentations. Meanwhile, the Portland Arms in South Lynn, previously labelled a local eyesore, was cleared for demolition to make way for an Anglian Water administration block.

Elsewhere, fire chiefs saw their request for smoke detectors in council homes rejected due to budget constraints, and concerns were raised regarding cliff erosion in Hunstanton. Additionally, the leaning walnut tree near the South Lynn post office was marked for felling due to safety fears, and American airforce personnel at RAF Sculthorpe were set to undergo mandatory AIDS screening.

stories.headline: Looking back at past community fundraising efforts in West Norfolk
stories.brief:
We are taking a look back at charitable events held across West Norfolk during past Septembers. In 2014, King’s Lynn’s Blue Watch firefighters raised over £360 for the Fire Fighters Charity by hosting a car wash. 

By September 2016, several local causes saw significant support. Staff from Goodwins Hall care home in Lynn raised £500 during a nine-kilometre walk for the Alzheimer’s Society. That same month, a Macmillan coffee morning at Knights’ Hill Great Barn collected £911, while a fashion show at Park House Hotel raised £4,250. Additionally, local author Bob Booth donated £750 to the East Anglian Air Ambulance, and a garden open day in Wimbotsham raised £400 for the Macmillan Centre at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital.

stories.headline: Fundraising appeal launched for new school equipment
stories.brief: A school is seeking to raise 80,000 pounds to pay for equipment in a new building. The appeal was reported by the Spalding South Holland News. Further details regarding the specific school or the timeline for the project have not been disclosed.

stories.headline: Thirteen young dogs rescued after being abandoned
stories.brief: Thirteen young dogs have been rescued after being left on the side of a road. The animals were discovered abandoned in an incident reported by the BBC. No further details regarding the location or the condition of the dogs have been released at this time.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn doctor struck off for misconduct
stories.brief:
A doctor who previously worked at Southgates Medical Centre and The Woottons Surgery has been removed from the medical register. The Medical Practitioners Tribunal Service found that Dr William Smerdon behaved inappropriately towards two mentally vulnerable patients. 

The tribunal heard that Dr Smerdon engaged in a sexual relationship with one patient and sexually harassed another between 2012 and 2019. The panel concluded that the doctor deliberately disregarded professional standards and showed a deep-seated attitudinal issue. While Dr Smerdon offered apologies during the hearing, the tribunal ruled that he must be erased from the register immediately, stating that the public would be appalled if he were allowed to continue practising as a GP.

stories.headline: Royal visit marks milestone at ARU Peterborough
stories.brief: A member of the Royal Family has visited ARU Peterborough to mark a significant milestone for the university. The event highlighted the institution's ongoing development and its role within the local area. Further details regarding the specific nature of the milestone or the identity of the royal visitor have not been released at this time.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire car thieves featured on Channel 4
stories.brief: A group of thieves from Cambridgeshire who were responsible for stealing vehicles valued at £500,000 are set to appear in a new Channel 4 programme. The criminals, who operated across the region, will be the subject of the upcoming television broadcast. Further details regarding the case and the specific programme schedule can be found in the latest report from the Ely East Cambridgeshire News.

stories.headline: Nearly 90 dogs seized from Spalding property
stories.brief: Authorities have removed almost 90 dogs from a property in Spalding. The animals were seized over the weekend following an operation at the site. No further details regarding the circumstances of the seizure or the current condition of the animals have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Tributes paid following fatal A142 crash in Chatteris
stories.brief: Tributes have been paid to a father who died following a road traffic collision on the A142 in Chatteris. Further details regarding the circumstances of the incident have not been released at this time.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn primary school rebrands as Parkway Academy
stories.brief:
Howard Junior School in Gaywood has officially been renamed Parkway Academy. The Eastern Multi-Academy Trust says the change marks a fresh start for the school following a consultation with staff, parents, and stakeholders. 

While the name has changed, the trust confirmed there will be no alterations to the current leadership, staff, or curriculum. The school has recently undergone a significant refurbishment, with all classrooms and the main hall redecorated and new learning spaces created. Chief executive Paul Shanks stated that the investment aims to provide an environment that reflects the ambition of the pupils and the wider community.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire Fire Service reports pressure from peat fires
stories.brief: Cambridgeshire Fire Service has reported that crews are currently under pressure due to a series of peat fires. The service has highlighted the ongoing situation as they work to manage the incidents across the region. Residents are advised to stay updated on local fire safety information as crews continue their efforts to tackle the blazes.

stories.headline: Approval granted for King’s Lynn HMO conversion
stories.brief:
Plans to convert a historic property in King’s Lynn into a house in multiple occupation have been approved by West Norfolk Council. The 1800s building, located at 70 London Road, is Grade II-listed and will be refurbished to provide four bedrooms. 

The project, submitted by Mr Mohamed, involves internal alterations including the installation of partition walls and a new shower room. A first-floor bathroom will be repurposed to create the additional bedroom. While the interior will undergo significant changes, the exterior of the building will remain largely untouched, with work limited to necessary window repairs.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire Combined Authority to review electric vehicle safety
stories.brief: The Cambridgeshire Combined Authority has announced plans to conduct a safety review regarding electric vehicles. The initiative, reported by the Ely Standard, will examine current standards and safety protocols for e-vehicles operating within the region. Further details on the scope of the assessment or the timeline for the review have not yet been released. Residents are advised to stay tuned for updates as the authority progresses with this evaluation.

stories.headline: Former March mayor expresses interest in buying town hall
stories.brief: A former mayor of March has announced plans to purchase the town hall. The proposal to acquire the local landmark was reported by the BBC. No further details regarding the potential sale or the intended future use of the building have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Wisbech hot food service saved by volunteers
stories.brief:
A weekly hot food outreach service in Wisbech has been saved from closure following a successful appeal for volunteers. The service, which has operated at the Salvation Army every Saturday evening for nearly four years, was at risk of shutting down due to a shortage of helpers. While the project is now secure for the foreseeable future, organisers are still seeking additional volunteers and donations of food items.

The service runs from 6pm to 7pm, with help needed for food preparation, serving, and cleaning. Volunteers do not need special experience or a weekly commitment. Those interested in donating ingredients or offering their time are asked to contact councillors Samantha Hoy or Steve Tierney via Facebook.

stories.headline: Progress for King’s Lynn swimming pool plans
stories.brief:
West Norfolk Council’s cabinet has approved spending £850,000 to develop designs for a new swimming pool and splashpad at the Lynnsport site. The proposed facility would replace the ageing St James Pool, which officials say is deteriorating. While the project could cost up to £23 million, the current funding will cover design work and a business case to determine if construction is viable.

Council leaders defended the expenditure, citing rising construction costs and the need to improve local water safety and swimming literacy. Some councillors have questioned the spending given there is no guarantee the pool will be built. The plans will now go before the full council, with a final decision on construction expected in early 2027.

stories.headline: Chatteris firefighters rescue dog from barbed wire
stories.brief: Fire crews in Chatteris have successfully rescued a dog that had become trapped in a barbed wire fence. The incident required intervention from local firefighters to safely free the animal from the wire. No further details regarding the condition of the dog or the exact location of the rescue have been released.

stories.headline: Historic King’s Lynn poster collection to be displayed this Sunday
stories.brief: A collection of 31 historic posters, preserved by former West Norfolk mayor Clifford Walters, will be exhibited this Sunday for King’s Lynn’s Heritage Open Day. The items, which date from 1791 to 1944, will be on display at the Chequer House Gallery on King Street. Mr Walters gathered the posters during his time as a councillor, including some discovered in the town hall. The King’s Lynn Civic Society has organised the event, and the first 200 visitors will receive a free commemorative booklet. Organisers hope the collection will eventually move to a permanent home at the Stories of Lynn museum.

stories.headline: New bereavement centre to open in Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: A new facility dedicated to bereavement support is set to open in Cambridgeshire. The centre, which will be known as Lake View, aims to provide services for those dealing with the loss of a loved one. Further details regarding the exact location and the range of support available are expected to be released as the project progresses.

stories.headline: Lincolnshire landlord fined for unsafe rental property
stories.brief: A landlord in Lincolnshire has been ordered to pay six thousand pounds following issues with an unsafe rental property. The case, reported by the Spalding South Holland News, highlights the legal consequences for failing to maintain safe living conditions for tenants. Further details regarding the specific location or the nature of the safety breaches have not been released.

stories.headline: Whittlesey Mayor invites residents to join pub crawl
stories.brief: The Mayor of Whittlesey, Paul Bristow, has extended an invitation to local residents to join him for a pub crawl. Details regarding the date, timing, or specific venues involved in the event have not been released. Residents are encouraged to keep an eye out for further information as it becomes available.

stories.headline: Simply Red tribute act to perform in Wisbech St Mary
stories.brief:
A tribute band dedicated to the music of Simply Red is set to perform in Wisbech St Mary next month. The act, known as Holding Back The Years, will appear at The Secret Garden on Saturday, September 12. The show is scheduled to run from 7.30pm until 10pm.

Organisers say the performance aims to recreate the atmosphere of a live Simply Red concert, featuring a lead vocalist and a full band. Tickets for the event are priced at £22 each. Those interested in attending can book their places online through the TicketSource website.

stories.headline: Large storage tanks arrive at King’s Lynn paper mill
stories.brief:
Large metal storage tanks were transported to the Palm Paper site on the Saddlebow Industrial Estate over the weekend. Police escorted the wide loads as they moved along the River Great Ouse and through King’s Lynn on Saturday and Sunday. 

The delivery is part of a major infrastructure project at the plant, which involves converting the site’s 10.6-metre-wide paper machine. Palm Paper recently announced it is shifting production away from newsprint to focus on manufacturing material for cardboard boxes. The company, which is one of West Norfolk’s largest employers, expects to begin production of the new corrugated material early next year.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire local government reorganisation plans paused
stories.brief: Proposed changes to the structure of local government in Cambridgeshire have been put on hold. Officials have confirmed that the plans are currently suspended while a formal review is carried out. No further details regarding the scope or expected duration of this review have been released at this time.

stories.headline: New treatment room opens at local salon
stories.brief: A beauty and holistic wellbeing salon has expanded its facilities. The business has officially opened a new treatment room for its clients. The development was reported by the Fenland Citizen.

stories.headline: Police appeal following serious collision in Whittlesey
stories.brief: Cambridgeshire Constabulary is appealing for information following a serious road traffic collision in Whittlesey. Officers are currently investigating the circumstances surrounding the incident. Anyone who may have witnessed the collision or who has relevant information is being urged to contact the police.

stories.headline: Rainbow Run returns to Peterborough’s Ferry Meadows
stories.brief: The annual Rainbow Run is making a comeback at Ferry Meadows in Peterborough. Organisers have confirmed the popular event will return to the park, offering participants the chance to take part in the colourful charity challenge once again. Those interested in joining the festivities are encouraged to look out for further details regarding registration and event timings. The run remains a staple fixture in the local calendar for the area.

stories.headline: Festive light show draws crowds to local church
stories.brief: A church in the Spalding area has hosted a popular light display, attracting a large number of visitors. The event featured a spectacular illumination show and gave attendees the opportunity to meet special festive guests. The gathering was reported by the Spalding South Holland News.

stories.headline: Fenland shop closed following police seizure
stories.brief: A shop in the Fenland area has been shut down by police. The closure follows the seizure of a quantity of cigarettes and vapes from the premises. No further details regarding the location of the shop or the timing of the operation have been released at this stage.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn founded charity expands support for bereaved military families
stories.brief:
A charity originally established in King’s Lynn is widening its reach to support adults affected by military-connected bereavement. Previously known as Scotty’s Little Soldiers, the organisation will now offer services to people of all ages, including veterans, reservists, and regular service personnel. 

Founded in 2010 by Nikki Scott, the charity confirms that children will remain a central focus of their work. The expansion aims to provide mental health support, social connections, and guidance to anyone grieving a death within the British Armed Forces community. Those seeking further information or support can contact the charity by calling 0800 092 8571 or emailing welcome@scottys.org.uk.

stories.headline: Two Cambridgeshire businesses under investigation for underage sales
stories.brief: Authorities are currently investigating two businesses in Cambridgeshire following allegations of underage sales. The inquiry into the firms is being conducted by local officials. No further details regarding the specific locations or the nature of the items sold have been released at this time.

stories.headline: E-scooter battery sparks house fire in Spalding
stories.brief: Fire crews in Spalding have identified the cause of a recent blaze at a residential property. Investigators confirmed that the fire was started by an e-scooter battery. Residents are reminded to remain cautious when charging lithium-ion devices within the home. No further details regarding the extent of the damage or any potential injuries have been released at this time.

stories.headline: New befriending scheme launched for care home residents
stories.brief: Age UK Cambridgeshire and Peterborough has introduced a new initiative aimed at supporting those living in care homes. The charity has launched a befriending scheme designed to provide companionship for residents across the region. Further details regarding how the programme will operate or how individuals can get involved have not yet been released. Residents and families interested in the service are encouraged to contact the local branch of Age UK for more information.

stories.headline: Moorfields Eye Hospital begins stem cell treatment trials
stories.brief: Moorfields Eye Hospital has launched clinical trials for a new stem cell treatment. The research focuses on a condition known as aniridia-related keratopathy, which affects the eyes. The Association of Optometrists has reported on the development, noting that the hospital is currently testing the effectiveness of this medical procedure. Further updates on the progress of these trials are expected as the study continues.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire eateries reach British Kebab Awards semi-finals
stories.brief: Several restaurants across Cambridgeshire have been named as semi-finalists in this year’s British Kebab Awards. The businesses are now in the running for national recognition in the competition. Further details regarding the specific local venues included in the shortlist have been reported by the Ely East Cambridgeshire News.

stories.headline: Lincolnshire pub owners announce closure due to burnout
stories.brief: The owners of a local pub have announced they are stepping down from the business. In a statement reported by the Spalding South Holland News, the proprietors explained that they have enjoyed their time running the establishment but are now suffering from burnout. They have decided to cut their losses and close the venue. No further details regarding the specific location of the pub or the date of the final service have been provided at this time.

stories.headline: March resident modifies sidecar for pet dog
stories.brief: A man living in March has completed a custom adaptation to his motorcycle sidecar. The modification was designed to accommodate his eight-year-old St Bernard. The project allows the large dog to travel alongside its owner.

stories.headline: Concerns raised over potential service changes at Queen Elizabeth Hospital
stories.brief:
Readers of the Lynn News have expressed significant concern regarding proposals to reduce services at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn. Correspondence published in the newspaper highlights fears that departments, including A&E, maternity, and intensive care, could be downgraded or moved. 

Residents have raised worries about the impact on patients, particularly those who may face long journeys to hospitals in Norwich, Cambridge, or Peterborough for urgent care. Concerns were also voiced regarding the pressure on local medical infrastructure due to the area's growing population and new housing developments. The debate follows ongoing discussions about the future functionality of the hospital as plans for a new facility continue.

stories.headline: Council rejects request for new crossing in March
stories.brief: Parents in March have expressed frustration after the local council turned down a proposal for a new school crossing. The decision has sparked anger among families who had campaigned for the safety measure. No further details regarding the specific location or the council's reasoning for the refusal have been provided at this time.

stories.headline: Springwood High School students mark end of Key Stage 3
stories.brief:
Students at Springwood High School in King’s Lynn have celebrated the completion of their Key Stage 3 studies. Year 9 pupils gathered at St Nicholas Chapel for a special presentation evening attended by the Mayor of West Norfolk, Councillor Steve Bearshaw, and school staff. 

More than 70 awards were handed out during the ceremony, recognising academic progress, attendance, and contributions to school life. Every Year 9 pupil received a certificate to mark the end of this phase of their education. Former student and current Oxford University undergraduate Mackenzie Whitehouse-Baker served as the guest speaker for the event, which was organised by Year 9 manager Sam Kempton.

stories.headline: New pedestrian crossing installed at Peterborough primary school
stories.brief: A new pedestrian crossing has been installed outside a primary school in Peterborough. The facility replaces the previous school crossing patrol service at the site. The change was reported by the BBC.

stories.headline: Government pauses decisions on Cambridgeshire local government reform
stories.brief: The government has announced a halt to decisions regarding local government reform in Cambridgeshire. The move has prompted reactions from local leaders across the county. Further updates on the status of these changes are expected as the situation develops.

stories.headline: Fenland shop closed following police seizure
stories.brief: A shop in the Fenland area has been shut down by police. The closure follows the seizure of a quantity of cigarettes and vapes from the premises. No further details regarding the specific location of the business or the timing of the operation have been released at this stage.

stories.headline: New £2 million pavilion opens at Wisbech Town Cricket and Hockey Club
stories.brief:
A new £2.03 million pavilion has officially opened at the Wisbech Town Cricket and Hockey Club on Harecroft Road. Club stalwart Jane Peggs performed the ribbon-cutting ceremony on Sunday in front of more than 300 guests. The facility features improved changing rooms, a bar, and social spaces designed for both sporting and community use.

While the building is now open, the club is continuing its Lasting Legacy crowdfunding campaign to raise a final £50,000. These funds will go towards completing the kitchen and bar areas, as well as furnishing the new social space. The campaign is currently scheduled to run until September 30.

stories.headline: Springwood High School students celebrate exam success
stories.brief:
Students from the Springwood High School Class of 2026 have marked the end of their school year with a special celebration in King’s Lynn. The graduates gathered at The Duke’s Head on Tuesday Market Place, which was transformed into a casino for the occasion. 

Dressed in formal evening wear, the students enjoyed a variety of entertainment including blackjack, roulette, arcade games, and a dance machine. The event, which was organised by heads of Year 13 Jess Cuss and Nicky Thompson, also featured a hot buffet and was attended by members of the school staff. The evening served as a final celebration of the students' exam achievements and their time together at the school.

stories.headline: Residents report sewage smell in Cambridgeshire market town
stories.brief: People living in a Cambridgeshire market town are reporting a persistent and unpleasant odour. According to reports, the area is currently being affected by what has been described as a foul stench of sewage. No further details regarding the source of the smell or any potential action being taken have been provided at this time.

stories.headline: Tilney St Lawrence man charged following King’s Lynn retail park incident
stories.brief:
A 24-year-old man from Tilney St Lawrence has been charged with drink-driving following reports of anti-social driving at the Hardwick Retail Park in King’s Lynn. Police were called to the site last Friday evening after receiving reports of vehicles drifting and performing handbrake turns.

Officers stopped a BMW at the scene, which was subsequently seized. The driver, Tom Perry of St John’s Road, was arrested and later charged with drink-driving. He has been bailed to appear at Lynn Magistrates Court on September 24. Norfolk Police have reminded the public that they have powers to seize vehicles involved in anti-social behaviour.

stories.headline: Police discover body in Peterborough search
stories.brief: Peterborough Police have confirmed that a body has been discovered during their search for a missing man. Officers made the find as part of an ongoing operation in the area. No further details regarding the identity of the individual or the circumstances surrounding the discovery have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Final protest held at Mepal crematorium site
stories.brief: A final protest has taken place at the site of the proposed Mepal crematorium. Charlotte Cane led the demonstration against the thirteen-million-pound project, which critics have labelled a white elephant. The development remains a point of contention for local residents as the campaign against the facility continues.

stories.headline: Police close shop following drug concerns
stories.brief: A shop has been closed by police due to concerns regarding drug dealing. The action was taken following reports linked to the premises. No further details regarding the location or the duration of the closure have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Wisbech veteran calls for review of state pension advice for ex-service personnel
stories.brief:
A Wisbech veteran is calling on the government to review how state pensions are managed for former service personnel. Mo Stewart, a former medical technician, claims she was incorrectly told in 2019 that she had to choose between her war pension and her state pension. 

The Department for Work and Pensions has apologised for the error and confirmed that its Complaint Resolution Team is investigating the matter urgently. Ms Stewart is now urging authorities to contact thousands of disabled war pensioners to ensure they are receiving their full entitlements. She is also calling for support for the families of deceased veterans who may have been misdirected regarding their pension claims in the past.

stories.headline: Man arrested following assault in King’s Lynn
stories.brief:
A man in his 20s has been arrested following an assault on Norfolk Street in King’s Lynn. Police were called to the scene shortly before 1am on Sunday morning after reports that a woman working at a business premises had been headbutted. The victim sustained a broken nose and a broken eye socket during the incident.

Officers are now appealing for any witnesses who have not yet come forward to get in touch. Anyone with information should contact Norfolk Police on 101, quoting crime reference 36/66935/26. Alternatively, information can be provided anonymously to the charity Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111.

stories.headline: Local school backs road safety campaign
stories.brief: A school has become the first to sign up for a new road safety initiative. The campaign, which is being promoted by LincsOnline, aims to improve safety standards on local routes. Further details regarding the specific school involved or the nature of the safety measures have not yet been released.

stories.headline: Government considers removing Neale-Wade Academy from Active Learning Trust
stories.brief: The Department for Education has warned it may remove the Neale-Wade Academy from the Active Learning Trust. This follows a critical inspection report from the education watchdog, Ofsted. The school, which is based in March, now faces potential changes to its management structure as a result of these findings. No further details regarding the timeline for these changes have been released at this stage.

stories.headline: Recent cases heard at King’s Lynn Magistrates’ Court
stories.brief:
A series of cases were heard at King’s Lynn Magistrates’ Court last Thursday. Among those sentenced, 49-year-old Antonio Vaz was fined for stalking after installing a tracking device in a partner’s handbag. 

In other matters, 47-year-old Clare Collins received a suspended prison sentence and a three-year driving ban for drink-driving, while 27-year-old Kane Curtis was disqualified for 12 months for a similar offence. Additionally, Kwok Wai Ho was handed 170 hours of unpaid work for driving while disqualified, and Ellie Marriott was fined for shoplifting and assault. Finally, an arrest warrant was issued for 21-year-old Harry Burley after he failed to appear at court for sentencing regarding a burglary charge.

stories.headline: Whittlesey shop closed following drug concerns
stories.brief: Police have closed a shop in Whittlesey due to concerns regarding drug dealing at the premises. Officers took action to shut the business following reports linked to illegal activity. No further details regarding the length of the closure or the specific location of the shop have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Five Cambridgeshire businesses named for underpaying staff
stories.brief: The government has publicly identified five businesses based in Cambridgeshire for failing to pay their staff the required legal minimum wage. The names were released following an official review into payroll practices across the region. While the specific identities of the companies have been disclosed by authorities, no further details regarding the scale of the underpayments or the sectors involved have been provided at this time. Residents are advised that the government continues to monitor local employers to ensure compliance with national wage regulations.

stories.headline: Retired vicar appointed to historic chivalric order
stories.brief: A retired vicar has been inducted into the oldest chivalric order in the country. The appointment was reported by the Spalding South Holland News. No further details regarding the identity of the individual or the specific order involved have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Whittlesey shop closed following drug concerns
stories.brief: Police have closed a shop in Whittlesey due to concerns regarding drug dealing at the premises. Officers took action to shut the business following reports linked to the site. No further details regarding the duration of the closure or the specific location of the shop have been released at this time.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn board game cafe celebrates first anniversary
stories.brief:
The Dice Box on Tower Street in King’s Lynn is marking its first year of business this weekend. Owners Chris Larwood and Stuart Walkley are hosting a birthday event on Saturday to celebrate the milestone. The cafe, which opened in 2025, offers a library of over 600 board games alongside LEGO, food, and drinks. 

Saturday’s celebration will feature giveaways, birthday cake, and a “roll for a discount” promotion for customers. The owners say they have welcomed thousands of visitors since opening and are inviting both experienced gamers and newcomers to join the festivities. Further details on the event and table bookings are available through the cafe’s social media pages.

stories.headline: Leicestershire children with learning disabilities missing eye care
stories.brief: New figures from the Association of Optometrists reveal that one in three children in Leicestershire with autism or a learning disability are not receiving necessary eye care. The data highlights a significant gap in service access for these young people. Health professionals are being urged to address these barriers to ensure children get the support they need for their vision.

stories.headline: Concerns raised over plans for nine-bedroom HMO in East Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: Residents have expressed concerns regarding a planning application for a nine-bedroom house in multiple occupation within East Cambridgeshire. The proposal, which has been reported by the Ely East Cambridgeshire News, is currently under scrutiny. No further details regarding the specific location or the nature of the objections have been provided at this stage.
